system.name: In-context algorithm selection (Post-ICL validation, Pre-ICL testing)
system.one_liner: Theory that one transformer can implement base in-context learning algorithms and select among them per input sequence, by post-ICL validation or pre-ICL testing.

content.variant_note: each example shows a black-box transformer's behaviour on two kinds of input; a thick curved arrow ties it to a dashed TF box that opens the mechanism as a bottom-up stack of stages; two such pairs sit side by side
content.argues: A single transformer can pick, per input sequence, which base algorithm or task to run, via validation losses after running algorithms or a distribution test before.
content.subject: Two examples of in-context algorithm selection and the two constructed mechanisms, post-ICL validation and pre-ICL testing, drawn inside the transformer.

lessons.what_to_learn: Pair a black-box behaviour (what the model does on two kinds of input) with the mechanism inside it: draw the mechanism as a dashed inner box of stacked stages and tie it back with one thick curved arrow; repeat the grammar for a second pair to put two mechanisms side by side.
lessons.suits: Theory or interpretability papers that construct a mechanism inside a model and want to show both the visible behaviour and the internal stages.

evidence: Figure 1 provides a pictorial illustration of the two mechanisms.
We construct two general mechanisms: Post-ICL validation, and Pre-ICL testing; See Figure 1 for a pictorial illustration.

summary: The paper gives a statistical theory of in-context learning in transformers, including in-context algorithm selection. Figure 1 shows the idea in two example-and-mechanism pairs split by a dotted rule. In Example 1 a single grey Transformer returns ridge regression with a different lambda for data with different noise; in Example 2 it returns linear regression for regression data and logistic regression for classification data. A thick curved arrow ties each to a dashed TF box that opens the mechanism as a bottom-up stack: train-validation split, K algorithms, K validation losses and a pick of the smallest (post-ICL validation), or a distribution test routing to K algorithms (pre-ICL testing).
summary_zh: 论文建立了Transformer上下文学习的统计理论，并证明其能在上下文中选择算法。图1分两组：左边展示单个Transformer在不同数据上给出不同算法的行为，粗弧线箭头连到虚线框，展开为验证式或检验式两种选择机制。
